classes.name: prior_override_failure
classes.signature: 0% pass rate on spec-divergent task; 100% after adding explicit example
classes.mechanism: The natural-language spec activates the canonical LeetCode-56 solution to merge_intervals, whose strict '<' does not merge touching intervals. When the spec states the touching rule explicitly, the model activates a different prior and writes '<=' on 20/20 trials. The mechanism is spec-driven prior selection, not code-level inability.

evidence.spec_divergence: canonical uses '<' (touching intervals not merged); spec requires '<='

rule_only_intervention.prompt: merge overlapping closed intervals AND intervals whose endpoints touch (the end of one equals the start of the next)
rule_only_intervention.note: Rule stated without an example — example was not necessary.

classes.remediation: State the divergent rule explicitly in the spec (e.g. 'the end of one equals the start of the next'). An example is not necessary. The failure is a spec-activation failure, not a test-matching failure.

classes.name: prior_override_failure
classes.signature: ~65% pass rate (pooled N=49, 95% CI [0.51, 0.77]) on spec-divergent task; 100% after explicit abs_tol specification
classes.mechanism: Model stochastically selects between the canonical idiom (math.isclose with default abs_tol=0.0) and a primitive implementation that satisfies the spec's 'handle zero safely' language. Rate depends on which reading the session lands on.

evidence.spec_divergence: canonical math.isclose defaults abs_tol=0.0; spec requires safe handling of zero-vs-tiny

rule_only_intervention.rule_text: absolute tolerance is a small nonzero value (not 0.0)

classes.remediation: State the divergent rule explicitly (nonzero absolute tolerance). Rule statement alone is sufficient; the specific numeric value is not required.

classes.name: under_specification_failure
classes.signature: 0.0 pass on ambiguous spec ('the index'); 1.0 pass on rule-stated spec ('the LEFTMOST index')
classes.mechanism: Spec uses a phrase ('the index') that has multiple valid interpretations. The canonical LeetCode-style solution to the general class (binary_search) returns any matching index, which satisfies one reading but not the one the test requires. The model is not violating a stated rule; it is filling an ambiguous spec with the canonical interpretation. When the ambiguity is resolved ('the LEFTMOST index'), the model writes the correct form.

evidence.original_spec: Write a Python function binary_search(arr, x) that returns the index of x in sorted arr, or -1 if absent.
evidence.rule_only_spec: Write a Python function binary_search(arr, x) that returns the LEFTMOST index of x in sorted arr (the smallest index if x appears more than once), or -1 if absent.

classes.remediation: Resolve the ambiguity in the spec. When the divergent reading is stated explicitly ('the LEFTMOST index'), the model writes the correct form.
classes.relationship_to_prior_override: Prior_override_failure: spec states the rule, model produces a code form that contradicts it. Under_specification_failure: spec admits two readings, model produces the canonical one, test requires the other. Both fixed by spec precision, but through different mechanisms.

control.interpretation: Test suite and tasks are clean; failures are model prior-specific, not capability gaps.

finding_inverse_scaling.statement: On spec-divergent tasks, the model with the strongest coding priors (gpt-oss-120b) fails at a higher rate than the weaker models, because the weaker models lack the offending prior.
finding_inverse_scaling.evidence: approximately_equal / original — pooled: 120b 32/49 (~65%); qwen 18/18 (100%); 20b 18/18 (100%). Inverse-scaling holds: the model with the strongest coding priors fails most often.

hypothesis_confirmed: Spec tightening eliminates prior_override_failure (both subtypes) at 100% across all affected cells.
qwen3.8-27b is a valid control: no failures on any cell.
revision_note: v1.1: stochastic rate revised from 0.444 (N=9) to 0.653 (pooled N=49) after tighten_rate.py produced 28/40. The mechanism is unchanged; only the magnitude.

conclusion.statement: All three failure classes (systematic prior_override, stochastic prior_override, and under_specification) are attributable to spec text activating a canonical solution that diverges from the test. Every class recovers to near-ceiling when the divergent requirement is stated explicitly in the spec.
conclusion.practical_implication: Benchmark spec text is not neutral. Every hedge word ('touching', 'the index', 'handle zero') activates a canonical prior that may contradict the test. Spec precision — even without test disclosure — recovers the failure by activating the correct prior. This suggests spec-writing standards for agent benchmarks: state divergent rules explicitly, avoid hedged adjectives when the test requires a specific interpretation.

recipe_validation.method: Three held-out tasks with canonical solutions were run on gpt-oss-120b with both ambiguous and recipe-intervention prompts, K=15 per cell, zero infra artefacts.

valid_palindrome.divergence: must filter non-alphanumeric and lowercase before comparison

majority_element.canonical: Boyer-Moore majority vote returns some candidate
majority_element.divergence: must return None when no majority element exists (>n/2)

isomorphic_strings.divergence: two-way mapping required; every character must map uniquely in both directions

findings.statement: Prior_override_failure requires that the canonical form be (a) common in the model's training data AND (b) genuinely contradict the spec. Both conditions held for valid_palindrome and majority_element, both failed to hold for isomorphic_strings.

The model already knows that isomorphic strings require bijective mapping. The one-way LeetCode-205 'naive' implementation is not the canonical form for this model. Recipe must be validated against the model's actual priors, not against assumptions about which solution is 'canonical'.

A pre-flight test (one ambiguous-prompt run) would have revealed that isomorphic_strings is not diagnostic before the 30-trial validation. Recipe step 1 ('detect canonical priors') should be a small batch of trials, not a static analysis.

recipe_validation.conclusion: Recipe is validated with a specificity constraint: prior_override_failure is only diagnostic when the canonical form is genuinely common AND genuinely contradicts the spec. Two of three held-out tasks confirmed the recipe; the third revealed the constraint that the recipe requires empirical prior verification, not static analysis.
